qs.q:
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

0. I've never seen such an extraordinary play. The actors contributed to the exceptional atmosphere. Everyone cheered with joy. [G = You should experience it.]
1. We headed towards Maksimir and realised we'd left the oven on. I know it's on your way from work, so please help out!
2. There's a new notice on the office board. It's very important that we understand the suggested changes. Don't forget to check it out tomorrow.
3. I tried to reach you by phone last week but I couldn't get through. You were unavailable. I'd like to hear from you.
4. Please do your homework before going to the book club, because you'll either be too tired or you'll forget about it.
5. It's been a while since you travelled. And dreaming big like studying in Australia is not far-fetched. I believe in you.
items: 1 — We left the oven on. It's on your way from work, so please help out!
2 — There's a new notice on the board. Don't forget to check it out tomorrow.
3 — I tried to reach you by phone but couldn't get through. I'd like to hear from you.
4 — Do your homework before going to the book club or you'll forget.
5 — Dreaming big like studying in Australia is not far-fetched. I believe in you.

qs.q:
Why is Gemma not attending the course during the holidays?

"I forgot to mention I'm flying to the Isle of Wight next month for a certified course in Graphic Design. I wanted to attend it last month but I was late, it was fully booked. I know it would be best to wait until the holidays, when it's cheaper, but you know me, I'm so impatient!"

A Because it was sold out.
B Because it was cheaper.
C Because she couldn't wait.

How many passengers arrived including Bella at the final stop?

"There was a blizzard and the train was delayed. First I was stuck in a carriage with a dozen other passengers and it was really stuffy, even when four of them got off and took the coach. When we started again, an elderly couple got on at the next stop and we were squeezed until we arrived at our destination."

A Four.
B Eleven.
C Twelve.

What did Lisa like about the exhibition?

"I loved the exhibition. What I liked was how many artists in the exhibition were exploring their dreams. They finally moved away from painting mythological scenes. The use of colour and non-traditional materials was absolutely brilliant. There was some confusion though about how the exhibits were displayed."

A It wasn't traditional.
B It was well-organised.
C It exhibited mythological themes.

What did Monica think of the concert?

"The Choones were amazing. Despite not having a solid voice, the singer appeared pretty sure of himself. He put on quite a show. I used to think their songs weren't catchy or romantic enough and preferred more soothing music like Colday. My sister changed my mind."

A She prefers a different kind of music.
B The singer's voice was disappointing.
C The singer's performance was impressive.
opts: She prefers a different kind of music.

qs.q:
What does Lara say about the cost of the dinner?

"The fish was absolutely mouth-watering. As for the price, it was reasonable, considering the exotic ingredients the master chef miraculously blended. We hoped it would be a bargain, since we know the restaurant owner, but we didn't mind."

A It was a bargain.
B It was expensive.
C It was medium-priced.

Reading aloud

"While fewer children start reading in preschool with the help of their teachers, the majority begin reading on their own very easily as a result of their parents reading to them."

Who helps most children start reading independently?
A They themselves.
B Their teachers.
C Their parents.

Reading aloud

"For reading aloud to be truly beneficial to children, the chosen stories must be interesting, realistic and inspiring for them."

What makes reading aloud helpful for children?
A Stories that are important to them.
B Stories that are motivating.
C Stories that are simple.
opts: Stories that are important to them.

qs.q:
Reading aloud

"Young children often struggle with concepts that are symbolic or abstract, such as those found in fantasy novels... Complex sentences and length can also sometimes be issues."

What do young readers find most challenging?
A Abstraction.
B Long stories.
C Language structures.

Reading aloud

"Puzzled by unfamiliar words, children will push themselves to learn because the words are important to the story."

How do children react when they first hear a new word?
A They ignore it.
B They feel confused.
C They are discouraged.

Reading aloud

"When children are encouraged to read what they want, they are motivated to read more."

How are good readers developed?
A By using digital tools.
B By building their vocabulary.
C By letting them choose their stories.
opts: By letting them choose their stories.

Read the message from Susan:

"Hi Peter,
I'm organising a surprise party for my friend, but I don't have much experience. Which party did you last go to and what was it like? What's the best place for a party and why? What do you think makes a great party? I really want it to be memorable.
Susan"

Write Susan a reply. Answer all her questions. Write 80–100 words.

You will hear five phone messages.
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

A — You should cooperate with them.
B — You've done everything possible.
C — I'll do whatever you want.
D — You can coordinate the activity.
E — I can help out.
F — Give yourself another chance.
rights: A — You should cooperate with them.
C — I'll do whatever you want.
D — You can coordinate the activity.
